walkthroughs.name: One requested change becomes one write

beats.heading: Callers state a transition
beats.body: The server constructs a pure transition from a create, edit, branch, settle, adopt, shelve or rename request, and hands it to the one write boundary.

beats.heading: The aggregate changes under one lease
beats.body: The write boundary takes the board's lease, rereads the file, checks the expected version, applies semantic edits and descendant reconciliation, then validates the complete candidate before advancing its version.

beats.heading: Drafts follow the edit in the same write
beats.body: An edit to a variant reaches every draft derived from it. Each draft is merged, left in conflict, or blocked behind an ancestor nobody has settled, and the whole family still lands as one version.

beats.heading: Success follows durable replacement
beats.body: Only the validated whole-board candidate reaches the file, moved first when its name changed; file and directory fsync complete before the applied result returns.

beats.heading: An old name keeps opening the board
beats.body: A rename keeps the old name as a former name and moves the file in the same write. Reads and writes ask which board a name answers to, so a link or a claim made under the old name reaches the board without any other board changing.

beats.heading: Letting a board go is a write too
beats.body: A discard takes the same lease and version check a write does, unlinks the file durably, and gives back the claim it ran under, so a board somebody changed meanwhile is kept.

variants.name: TASK-549.03 integration
variants.summary: Durable canonical edits on the adopted refactored architecture

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Every write of a board comes through it, and every read but the command line's search for the vaults that hold a checkout's boards

nodes.name: Address and locate
nodes.responsibility: Maps names to safe vault paths
nodes.description: semanticBoardAddress normalizes board identity without I/O; locateSemanticBoard resolves the .semantic.json file and follows existing ancestors to refuse symlink paths that leave the configured vault.

nodes.name: List boards
nodes.responsibility: Discovers semantic board files
nodes.description: Recursively enumerates semantic board locations to a bounded depth, recognizing only .semantic.json aggregates and preserving their nested board names.

nodes.name: Read and validate
nodes.responsibility: Reads a coherent aggregate from disk, by its name or a name it used to have
nodes.description: readSemanticBoard asks Former names which board a name answers to; readSemanticBoardAt synchronously reads fresh bytes, asks Decode board bytes to parse and migrate the shared semantic schema, distinguishes missing from unreadable files, and rejects a document whose internal name disagrees with its address. A document of an older contract is migrated, and persisted when its lease is free, before it is answered. readSemanticBoardAtAsLeased, for a question asked before a write, answers a board that awaits its migration as the migration would leave it, at the version the migration commits, and persists nothing.

nodes.name: Lifecycle transitions
nodes.responsibility: Defines board lifecycle changes
nodes.description: Factories return pure create, edit, branch, settle, adopt and shelve transitions; a rename is its own transition. An edit may also restate the summary and the document references of the variant it lands on, in the same write, and is refused on a historical or shelved variant as a content edit is. A branch copies the document references of the variant it comes from (ADR 0054). The write boundary executes the chosen transition against the board read under lease.

nodes.name: Edit semantic content
nodes.responsibility: Resolves names into stable subjects
nodes.description: editContent, editViews, and editWalkthroughs plan removals, mint identifiers centrally, resolve same-write handles and references, preserve replacement semantics, and refuse orphaned containment or stranded narrative references.

nodes.name: Propagate descendant edits
nodes.responsibility: Carries parent changes into drafts
nodes.description: propagateEdit walks descendants of an edited variant, automatically merges compatible changes, records reconciliation issues where meanings diverge, and blocks descendants behind unresolved ancestors.

nodes.name: Settle disagreements
nodes.responsibility: Answers the disagreements a proposal holds and carries the answer down
nodes.description: settleVariant applies explicit reconciliation choices and ordering decisions; an ordinary edit that restores what a proposal removed settles through the same catch-up. A draft waiting on the answer is merged in the same write and reports what it finds.

nodes.name: Write under lease
nodes.responsibility: Commits one durable version
nodes.description: writeSemanticBoard locates the target, takes the board-wide lease under the writer's claim or an identity minted for the write, runs Check a candidate on the board it reads under that lease, and persists the candidate once, at the next version. writeSemanticBoardAt stamps the write at an instant a caller states, which is how a prepared candidate lands as the board that was prepared.

nodes.name: Atomic file replacement
nodes.responsibility: Fsyncs every change to a board file: a replacement, a move and an unlink
nodes.description: writeFileAtomic writes a temporary sibling, fsyncs file content, renames it over the destination, and fsyncs the directory; moveFileDurably and unlinkDurably sync the directory the same way, so accepted board writes are committed before callers receive success.

nodes.name: Vault diagnostics
nodes.responsibility: Everything wrong with the vault's boards, as warnings a repair can answer

nodes.name: Drill-down checks
nodes.responsibility: What a board can say about a link to another one, checked across the whole vault and, for a link that names a repository, the vault of that repository
nodes.description: A link is the one thing on a board that names something outside it, so no single board can check it: a node with nothing but its link, a board the vault does not hold, and a kind that disagrees with the level it opens (ADR 0029). A link that names a repository identity (ADR 0049) asks the same of the vault of that identity's chosen checkout, reading the target board there without migrating it, and adds two questions: whether this machine has a checkout of the repository at all, and whether the board there can be read. A link that names the vault's own repository stays in the vault, as the board listing reads it.

nodes.name: Replaced relationships
nodes.responsibility: Warns when a write may have lost a relationship's identity: re-added under a new id, or stated twice
nodes.description: A write that breaks a continuing relationship's identity is not refused: the board is valid, so the write lands and its answer carries RELATIONSHIP_REPLACED or RELATIONSHIP_DUPLICATED naming the repair. An explicit removeEdges plus an idless addition declares a replacement and draws no notice.

nodes.name: Adopt
nodes.responsibility: Makes a settled draft current, or gives a board nobody had built its first current variant; refuses a draft derived from an architecture a later adoption superseded unless forced
nodes.description: Adoption renames nothing and rewrites no history: the variant that was current becomes a historical state under its own name. On a board with no current variant nothing becomes history (ADR 0031). A draft standing on a historical variant would drop what was adopted over it, so it is refused as PARENT_SUPERSEDED unless the request forces it, and the adoption record then says it was forced (ADR 0037).

nodes.name: Shelve
nodes.responsibility: Lets a proposal go without deleting it, so every link that names it still opens it
nodes.description: Shelving changes nothing the variant says; the board records that nobody intends to carry it out (ADR 0030).

nodes.name: Rename
nodes.responsibility: A pure transition that moves one name, the board's or a variant's, and keeps the old one as a former name
nodes.description: Every id, lifecycle, ancestry and record of adoption stays as it was (TASK-281, ADR 0036).

nodes.name: Former names
nodes.responsibility: Which board a name answers to: the board that carries it, else the one that used to
nodes.description: A board's own name always wins. Only a miss looks through the vault's formerNames, so a drill-down, a saved pane address or a command written before a rename keeps opening the board it meant; nothing is cached (ADR 0036).

nodes.name: Place the file
nodes.responsibility: Writes the board's file where its name puts it, moving it there first when a rename changed that name
nodes.description: A new name is taken under its own lease as well, without waiting, and refused when another board carries it or used to. A write that fails after the move puts the file back, so a refused rename leaves the vault as it was.

nodes.name: Discard
nodes.responsibility: Removes a whole board under the lease and version check a write takes, refused while another board of the vault opens it; answers its tracked embeds and gives back its claim
nodes.description: semantic delete (TASK-526.06, ADR 0057) and semantic record --discard (TASK-304.02). BOARD_OPENED_BY names each node on a current or draft variant that opens the board by its name or a former name; history and shelved proposals do not refuse, and another repository's vault cannot be seen. The note holds the name and the former names, so they are free afterwards. A board somebody else holds is refused with the words a write gets.

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: a lease file beside the board, an agent's claim on it, and who holds it
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives in the vault, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion; a dead holder costs one lease rather than wedging the board. A person's take-back (takeBackBoard) holds the lease with the claim revoked and gives it straight back, and answers the claim that stood. The claims, the lock watch and the lines agents said they were doing are process memory, and forgetBoardMemory drops all of it when a server stops, leaving the leases in each vault as they are.

nodes.name: Binding checks
nodes.responsibility: A node on the current variant whose binding names a file the repository no longer has

nodes.name: Vault configuration
nodes.responsibility: Reads the vault's vocabulary and appearance from its config.yaml, and seeds that file in a new vault

nodes.name: Dropped anchors
nodes.responsibility: Says which relationships and steps a write restated without the anchor they had
nodes.description: A write that restates a relationship or a flow step under its id without the anchor it had is not refused: the board is valid without it, so the write lands and its answer carries ANCHOR_DROPPED with the anchor spelled out for the next write to put back. A subject the batch did not state keeps its anchor.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Reads Git history through a board's bindings without changing the vault: footprints and hotspots take a board and variants by name and choose the variants they read

nodes.name: Decode board bytes
nodes.responsibility: Parses and migrates a board document entirely in memory

nodes.name: Vault checkouts
nodes.responsibility: Which checkout holds each repository identity for one vault, and which identity the vault's own checkout holds
nodes.description: The one rule that every reader of a vault resolves a repository identity by (ADR 0049): the vault's own checkout for its own identity, the chosen checkout for any other. The binding checks use it to find a bound file, and the drill-down checks use it to find the vault a link into another repository opens, and to tell a link that names the vault's own repository from one that leaves it.

nodes.name: Move
nodes.responsibility: Moves a whole board, every variant, former name and id, into another repository's vault: the target note first, then each rewritten drill-down, the source note deleted last
nodes.description: ADR 0051, TASK-472.15. Holds the board's lease in the source vault, then its name's lease in the target without waiting. checks.ts refuses a same repository, a taken name and a link needing an untracked identity; drill-downs.ts rewrites the links in both vaults. checkedMove runs those checks and rewrites in memory, reading the board through the reader its caller gives it (under the lease by default), and the move writes what it found; Move preview runs it alone. A move that stopped part way leaves the board in both vaults, and running it again finishes it. It gives back the claim it ran under.

nodes.name: Move preview
nodes.responsibility: Says what a move would rewrite, or why it would be refused, holding and writing nothing
nodes.description: TASK-472.16, ADR 0051. Runs the move's own checks and rewrites against the two vaults as they are on disk, then answers the board, both ends and every drill-down it would rewrite, each as it would read. A writer is never kept waiting for a question, so the answer can be out of date by the time the move runs: the move checks everything again under its leases, and the version the preview read is the one the move states.

nodes.name: Board reading
nodes.responsibility: Finds a board by its name or a former name, lists the boards of a vault, reads and validates one from disk, and reads the vault configuration its vocabulary comes from

nodes.name: Board transitions
nodes.responsibility: The pure half of a change: turns a stated command into a candidate board, reconciles descendants and settles disagreements, and answers a write with what it lost

nodes.name: Durable writes
nodes.responsibility: Commits a board change, a discard or a move under the lease and version check of each board it writes, and writes each file where its name puts it

nodes.name: Vault checks
nodes.responsibility: Reports everything wrong with the boards of a vault as warnings: configuration problems, drill-down links that lead nowhere, and bindings whose file is gone

nodes.name: Board move
nodes.responsibility: Moves a whole board to another repository's vault in a fixed order, and previews what the move would rewrite without writing

nodes.name: Command dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards directly once: in a checkout with no vault, to name the known vaults that hold boards of its code

nodes.name: Bound vaults
nodes.responsibility: Which known vaults hold boards that bind one repository's code, read without a lease and without a write
nodes.description: TASK-480. The known vaults are the ones the navigator lists: the vault of each chosen checkout and each untracked vault that exist. A board counts when a node of any variant binds the repository. A board that needs a migration is migrated in memory only, because the vault belongs to another repository.

nodes.name: Historical corrections
nodes.responsibility: Corrects historical meaning against immutable revisions, reconciles inheriting drafts and preserves adopted successors

nodes.name: Check a candidate
nodes.responsibility: What every write passes before a file changes: the board read, the stated version checked, the change applied and the candidate admitted
nodes.description: checkedCandidate reads the board through a reader its caller chooses, refuses a change that states no version or the wrong one, applies the transition, finds where the name puts the file, and admits the result under the vault's vocabulary and the board's own address. It takes no lease and writes nothing. The write pass runs it under the lease, a prepared write runs it with a read that holds none, and a discard and a move use boardBefore for the same version check.

nodes.name: Prepare a write
nodes.responsibility: Makes the candidate a write would land with no lease held, and commits exactly that candidate afterwards
nodes.description: prepareSemanticBoardWrite reads the board as its lease would, applies a stated transition or a historical correction, and admits the candidate by the rules a write itself uses. Its answer carries a commit bound to that candidate: the commit writes the prepared board at the prepared instant under the lease and refuses BOARD_VERSION_CONFLICT when the board has moved since, so the subject ids a caller read evidence about are the ids written. A change to a board that does not exist is refused BOARD_MISSING.

nodes.name: Carry a rename
nodes.responsibility: Writes a rename, then carries this server's claim and the lines agents wrote to the board's new name
nodes.description: renameSemanticBoard states the rename as a transition and writes it. When the write moved the board to a new name, the lines agents wrote about the board stay with it and this server's claim follows, for the reason it was taken. A claim that could not follow adds a CLAIM_NOT_CARRIED warning to the answer. The server only points its panes at the new name.

nodes.name: Read a variant
nodes.responsibility: Reads a board by name and opens the variant an address states
nodes.description: readBoardVariant reads the board by its name or a former name, then opens the variant the address states: an id, a name or current. A bare name, an empty variant and current all open what the bare name opens. When the address opens no variant the answer carries the board it read and says whether the variant is missing or the name chooses none.

nodes.name: Track an embed
nodes.responsibility: A pure transition that lists one tracked embed on the board, once, and changes no variant, so it needs no stated version
nodes.description: ADR 0057. The list is the board's, so behind's last change does not move for it, and a move carries it with the note.

nodes.name: Move checks
nodes.responsibility: Asks the vaults of a move which names are taken and which drill-downs open the board, as they are on disk; a delete asks it which drill-downs open the board

nodes.name: Canonical model read
nodes.responsibility: Reads one coherent authored model with exact path and byte revisions
nodes.description: Decodes captured architecture through shared schemas and coherence rules. Current reads capture paths and exact bytes twice. Retained reads reuse its decoder and module selection without opening current files. Pending canonical installation blocks a current read with recovery instructions.

nodes.name: Canonical model contracts
nodes.responsibility: Defines canonical inputs, exact revisions, checkpoint metadata and shared outcomes

nodes.name: Canonical checkpoint operations
nodes.responsibility: Retains exact current architecture and reads or lists immutable checkpoints
nodes.description: Expected revisions and operation identities protect retention. Retries return the same checkpoint. Exact reads use retained policy and modules only. Unavailable source evidence stays separate from missing architecture. Its shared result projection and structured refusal mapping also serve canonical edits, claims and recovery.

nodes.name: Canonical archive objects
nodes.responsibility: Stores architecture-only Git objects and joins concurrent archive ancestry
nodes.description: Configured identity and signing govern checkpoints and marked synchronization commits. Required checkpoints remain actual Git parents. Retention refs preserve operations before conditional archive appends. Common Git objects and refs serve linked worktrees without changing current files, index or HEAD.

nodes.name: Git process commands
nodes.responsibility: Runs supervised Git processes with exact input and optional untrimmed object output

nodes.name: Legacy board writes
nodes.responsibility: Validates, writes, and moves legacy board documents

nodes.name: Legacy migration planning
nodes.responsibility: Inventories exact legacy inputs and records explicit identity choices without changing live architecture
nodes.description: Reads original documents and policy without persisting schema upgrades. Names, bindings and drill-downs supply evidence only. An atomic mapping plan retains namespaces, aliases, choices and unresolved conflicts under source and plan fingerprints.

nodes.name: Migration planning contracts
nodes.responsibility: Defines original inventory, qualified identity mappings and source-bound conflict choices

nodes.name: Canonical edit operations
nodes.responsibility: Applies an explicit description intent or returns its signed durable result
nodes.description: Same-operation retries can read completion without the installation lease or current inputs. New edits and recovery use the shared checkout-private transaction boundary.

nodes.name: Canonical architecture
nodes.responsibility: Reads, retains and edits one canonical model with durable recovery

nodes.name: Canonical edit preparation
nodes.responsibility: Validates one complete candidate and signs its checkpoint before installation
nodes.description: Preserves exact unrelated bytes and checks the full read token, target state and subject claim again after signing.

nodes.name: Canonical installation
nodes.responsibility: Resumes exact logged images and completes retention before announcing a write
nodes.description: Preserves foreign bytes and refuses changed branch context. Prepares archive synchronization signing before file installation. A conditional append conflict leaves recovery work instead of invoking a signer after file changes.

nodes.name: Canonical recovery state
nodes.responsibility: Keeps a durable journal and short installation lease in the checkout private Git directory
nodes.description: The current reader refuses unfinished installation. Linked worktrees keep separate journals and branch context. Durable completed results remain readable while cleanup is pending.

nodes.name: Canonical subject claims
nodes.responsibility: Claims explicit module identities and records release or reader take-back
nodes.description: A claim names the writer, purpose, target and time. It leaves the short installation lease free during agent work. Take-back refuses the former claim on its next edit.

nodes.name: Canonical model subscription
nodes.responsibility: Sends a fresh coherent snapshot and observes valid external changes without adoption
nodes.description: Each connection receives current reading and claims. Completion, external observations, unavailable reads and claim changes use shared public event payloads. Historical reads stay independent.

nodes.name: Canonical local news
nodes.responsibility: Notifies local subscribers after durable operations release their lease
nodes.description: Disk observation covers other processes. Observer failures cannot undo an accepted edit.

nodes.name: Canonical operation contracts
nodes.responsibility: Defines explicit edit targets, complete read tokens, claims, recovery outcomes and wire events

walkthroughs.name: One requested change becomes one write

beats.heading: Callers state a transition
beats.body: The server constructs a pure transition from a create, edit, branch, settle, adopt or shelve request and hands it to the one write boundary. A rename goes to the board package, which states the transition itself and carries the claim and the lines agents wrote to the new name. The server only points its panes.

beats.heading: The aggregate changes under one lease
beats.body: The write boundary takes the board's lease, rereads the file, checks the expected version, applies semantic edits and descendant reconciliation, then validates the complete candidate before advancing its version.

beats.heading: Drafts follow the edit in the same write
beats.body: An edit to a variant reaches every draft derived from it. Each draft is merged, left in conflict, or blocked behind an ancestor nobody has settled, and the whole family still lands as one version.

beats.heading: Success follows durable replacement
beats.body: Only the validated whole-board candidate reaches the file, moved first when its name changed; file and directory fsync complete before the applied result returns.

beats.heading: An old name keeps opening the board
beats.body: A rename keeps the old name as a former name and moves the file in the same write. Reads and writes ask which board a name answers to, so a link or a claim made under the old name reaches the board without any other board changing.

beats.heading: Letting a board go is a write too
beats.body: A discard takes the same lease and version check a write does, unlinks the file durably, and gives back the claim it ran under, so a board somebody changed meanwhile is kept.

beats.heading: A candidate can be read before it lands
beats.body: A historical correction must read the code at the revisions it cites before it may land, and reading Git must not hold the board. So the store prepares the candidate with no lease, by the checks a write passes, and commits exactly that candidate later under the lease. The commit reads the board again and refuses the write when the version moved, so the subject ids the evidence was read for are the ids written.
